changes.location: Executive Summary › paragraph 2
changes.before: Secure Score provides useful evidence of Microsoft-reported control status, but it is not a measure of overall risk or control effectiveness. These areas remain unassessed rather than being presumed secure or unchanged.

changes.location: Executive Summary › paragraph 3

changes.location: Executive Summary › paragraph 4
changes.before: Overall Secure Score is 61.74% (163 of 264 points), compared with 60.00% (159 of 265) in Q2 and 58.49% (155 of 265) in Q1. changes.after: Overall Secure Score rose from 60.00% (159 of 265) in Q2 to 61.74% (163 of 264 points) in Q3, and Q1 was 58.49% (155 of 265). changes.location: Security Signal Review › Data Protection and Collaboration › paragraph 2
changes.before: Material native gaps concern phishing thresholds, user and domain impersonation, associated intelligence-based actions, safety tips and custom anti-phishing policy. Mailbox intelligence is complete at 8/8, but its separate impersonation actions are not. Safe Links for email is 9/9 while Office applications is 0/3. Other open actions cover MailTips, Outlook add-ins, spam notifications, 30-day quarantine, bulk complaint threshold and blocking users at the message limit. Broader forwarding restriction is 0/5 despite system-controlled forwarding at 1/1. Customer Lockbox remains open even though the required license is available, while data-map labels and auto-labeling are not currently supported by the available licensing. Taken together with the completed DLP recommendation, this indicates that HHA has established part of its data protection foundation but does not yet have clear evidence that protection and labeling coverage extends across the intended business scope. HHA should prioritize enabling Customer Lockbox, and review where sensitive information is stored and shared, and determine whether broader labeling capabilities are needed based on business and regulatory requirements rather than Secure Score alone.
changes.after: The material native gaps concern phishing thresholds, user and domain impersonation, associated intelligence-based actions, safety tips, and the custom anti-phishing policy. Other open actions cover MailTips, Outlook add-ins, spam notifications, 30-day quarantine, the bulk complaint threshold, and blocking users at the message limit. Broader forwarding restriction is 0/5, although system-controlled forwarding is 1/1. Customer Lockbox remains open even though the required license is available, while data-map labels and auto-labeling are not supported by the licensing available in Q3. Together with the completed DLP recommendation, these results indicate that HHA has established part of its data protection foundation but lacks clear evidence that protection and labeling coverage extends across the intended business scope. observations.location: Security Signal Review › Identity and Access › evidence table
observations.detail: The identity evidence table lists control points of 10/10, 9/9, 8/8, 4/4, 0/1, and two 7/7 credits. These are components of the reported Identity total of 65/66 but do not reconcile to it on their own, so the table is not an exhaustive breakdown of the Identity score.

observations.location: Security Signal Review › Identity and Access › paragraph 2 and evidence table › row: Risk policies
observations.detail: The prose states that the risk-policy credit shows no applicable license and does not establish deployed Entra ID P2 policies. The table states that the recommendation is complete due to Entra Security Defaults. The draft does not establish which explanation applies.

observations.location: Recommended Security Actions › Security Awareness call-out
observations.detail: The Security Awareness call-out refers to ASM’s evidence rather than HHA. The call-out is exempt from rewriting and was preserved unchanged.

observations.location: Recommended Security Actions › Security Awareness call-out versus Security Signal Review › AI Agents and Generative AI Usage
observations.detail: The Security Awareness call-out states that discovery confirms access to multiple AI services, while the AI section states that no AI usage inventory or governance evidence was available. The call-out also names identity recovery as an awareness topic that the Identity section does not discuss.

observations.location: Recommended Security Actions › Active Recommendations and CIS Microsoft 365 Foundation Benchmark › Status column
observations.detail: The template requires the status format MM.DD.YYYY - <STATUS DESCRIPTION>. The draft supplies no per-item dates, so the draft status wording was retained.

observations.location: Recommended Security Actions › Active Recommendations › Identified column
observations.detail: The template uses the format YYYY.QQ for the identification quarter. The draft uses the format 2026 Q1 and 2026 Q3, and the draft values were retained.

observations.location: Security Signal Review › Endpoint and Vulnerabilities, Cloud Workload and Attack Path Exposure, and AI Agents and Generative AI Usage
observations.detail: The template places a separate conclusion paragraph at the end of each of these sections. The draft states the limitation in its introductory and supporting paragraphs and has no separate conclusion paragraph, so none was added.

observations.location: Current Microsoft Cloud Security Posture › Domain Posture › introduction
observations.detail: The template states that indicators are carried forward from the previous assessment. The draft states that no prior indicator is carried forward without validation, and the draft wording was retained.

observations.location: Domain Posture and Security Signal Review evidence tables
